correctness.rationale: Factor presence with one 1 is exactly a southwest union of rectangles with corners (a,b),(b,c),(c,d); with two 1s only inner gap b or c is possible and rectangle corners are (a,c),(b,d). Minimal absence is absence with present length-(m-1) prefix/suffix. The zero-one count classification covers 0..4 ones, and every omitted higher-one candidate has an absent proper factor. Counting frontier drops yields |MAW|≤K+13 where K=min(max(a,b,c),max(b,c,d)); if the sum s of three nonmaximal gaps is ≥11, this is < n. For s≤10, the verified finite base of 4×3×C(13,3)=3432 cases plus a rigorously justified eventual affine dependence for the single large gap reduces all lengths to bounded checks. Independent direct substrings/MAW enumerator for all three-one words n=7..14 found max count n and exactly two extremizers, 110^(n-3)1 and 10^(n-3)11. Actual VERIFY.py source inspection shows the full finite certificate and separate direct classification checks.
residual_risks: The 3432-case base and affine-ray lemma are both required; finite n≤14 independently corroborates but does not exhaust all lengths.

value.rationale: Minimal absent factors form a natural antifactor basis used in text algorithms and compressed representations; fixing three isolated markers gives a meaningful sparse-string subclass. The full zero-gap structural classification, exact maximum n at every n≥7 and exhaustive equality conditions constitute a natural complete classification and sharp cutoff, not an arbitrary small case.
residual_risks: No result for weight≥4, nonbinary alphabets or scattered subsequences; the polynomial-time finite base must be retained to make the proof fully reproducible.

limitations: Binary words of exactly three ones; complete classification all n≥3 and sharp equality theorem only n≥7. Finite certificate supports residual bounded cases; no claim for other Hamming weights.
